title: Flatness modulo all powers of an ideal implies flatness (Noetherian case)
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a ring map of commutative rings, $I\subseteq R$ an ideal and $M$ an $S$-module (an $R$-module via $\varphi$). Assume (1) $R$ is a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; (2) $S$ is a Noetherian ring; (3) $M$ is a finitely generated $S$-module; (4) for every $n\ge1$ the module $M/I^nM$ is flat over $R/I^n$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then for every prime $\mathfrak q\subseteq S$ containing $IS$ (the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(I)$) the localization $M_{\mathfrak q}$ is a flat $R$-module. In particular, if $S$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_S$ and $IS\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, then $M$ is a flat $R$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0523 (lemma-flat-module-powers, line 23807); its proof uses Lemma Tag 00ML (lemma-variant-local-criterion-flatness), Remark lemma-Tor-ring-mod-ideal and Lemma Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module, Artin-Rees)
